country.comment: The empirical analysis examines municipalities in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 3, Section 1; PDF p. 9, Section 4.1

effect_estimate.comment: Across 572 Minas Gerais municipalities, regulatory inspection (August 2020) and consolidation of social tariff rules (Regulation No. 150/2021) were associated with roughly a 19 percentage-point increase in the Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff (DIST Index) in 2020-2021 random-effects GLS models and roughly a 13 percentage-point increase in 2018-2021 robustness models. Municipal Sanitation Fund governance (MSF) had no statistically significant effect (coefficients 0.2286 to 0.3314, p > 0.10), travel time to the state capital was negatively associated (-0.4632 to -0.4781, p < 0.05), CadUnico update rate had a small negative association (-0.3571 to -0.3809, p < 0.01), and log population (1.8832, p < 0.01), log elementary-educated CadUnico enrollees (1.8794, p < 0.05), and log broadband connections (1.2769, p < 0.01) were positively associated with implementation.
effect_estimate.value: Mean municipal Degree of Implementation of the Social Tariff (DIST Index) rose from 68.28% (SD 24.76%) in 2020 to 87.53% (SD 15.13%) in 2021 across N = 572 municipalities (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank Z = -17.557, p = 0.000; positive increases in 419/572 [73.3%] municipalities, significant in all 12 macro-regions at p <= 0.004; municipalities with DIST < 50% fell from 151/581 to 17/583). In balanced random-effects GLS panel regressions (N = 572 municipalities, 1,144 observations, 2020-2021), regulation and enforcement (REGU) increased the DIST Index by 19.2078 percentage points (SE = 0.8174, p < 0.01) in Model 1, 19.155 (SE = 0.8143, p < 0.01) in Model 2, and 18.819 (SE = 0.8101, p < 0.01) in Model 3. In 2018-2021 robustness panel models (N = 570 municipalities, 2,280 observations, DIST on 0-1 scale), REGU increased DIST by 0.1345 (SE = 0.0059, p < 0.01), 0.1348 (SE = 0.0059, p < 0.01), and 0.1313 (SE = 0.0060, p < 0.01).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 7-9, Section 2.2; PDF pp. 13-18, Sections 5.1-5.4, Tables 3, 4, 5, and 6

mechanism_certainty.comment: Assigned 2 rather than 3 because, although evaluated under ROBINS-I as a non-randomized intervention study, the before-and-after panel design lacks an untreated concurrent control group (REGU is a post-intervention year dummy, yielding Serious risk of bias for secular time-varying confounding, as illustrated by the 2020 dip noted in footnote 16). Within the <=2 ceiling, 2 is warranted because the paper directly observes and documents the administrative and regulatory enforcement process (CadUnico list selection, surprise regulatory audits, corrective utility actions, Regulation No. 150/2021, and municipal billing registration records).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 6-9, Sections 2.1-3; PDF pp. 13-18, Sections 4.3-5.4; PDF p. 20, Section 7

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines social tariff eligibility rules based on CadUnico registration and two-year recertification updates (ELIGIBILITY, documentation), means-tested ~50% tariff discounts for low-income households (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, fees, hardship_exception, accommodation), administrative registration procedures including automatic list transfers vs online/app customer requests and physical distance to capital bureaucracy (BURDEN, procedural_steps), regulatory inspections and compliance monitoring by Arsae-MG (ENFORCEMENT, administrative_review), Municipal Sanitation Funds/Councils (participation), and state-municipal-utility coordination, outreach campaigns, and CadUnico enrollment support (political_coordination, bureaucratic_assistance).

outcome_flags.comment: The study measures municipal implementation of the water and sewage social tariff (~50% bill reduction designed to achieve WSS affordability for low-income connected households) via the DIST Index, defined as the share of eligible low-income CadUnico households successfully registered/enrolled as social tariff beneficiaries in the utility billing database (capturing both affordability subsidy reach and beneficiary enrollment/application success). Physical network connection is an eligibility prerequisite rather than a measured outcome.
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 4-9, Sections 2.1-3; PDF pp. 13-18, Section 5

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: The study is a non-randomized longitudinal intervention evaluation testing the effect of a specific regulatory intervention (Arsae-MG inspections and Regulation No. 150/2021) using pre-post municipal panel regressions and paired Wilcoxon tests. ROBINS-I applies to non-randomized intervention studies; note that the authors explicitly report having no concurrent untreated counterfactual group (precluding difference-in-differences), which places the study at Serious risk of bias for time-varying confounding under ROBINS-I.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF pp. 12-13, Sections 4.2-4.4; PDF p. 20, Section 7

sample_size.comment: Raw Arsae-MG inspection reports covered 581 municipalities in 2020 and 583 municipalities in 2021; 9 municipalities with additional service providers besides Copasa-MG and Copanor were excluded to yield the balanced main panel of 572 municipalities (1,144 observations), and 2 further municipalities lacking 2018 DIST data were excluded in the 4-year robustness panel of 570 municipalities (2,280 observations).
sample_size.value: 572 municipalities (1,144 municipality-year observations, 2020-2021; >600,000 households registered in the social tariff) in main panel; 570 municipalities (2,280 municipality-year observations, 2018-2021) in robustness check
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 9-13, Sections 4.1 and 4.4; Table 1, PDF p. 12; Table 5, PDF p. 16; Table 6, PDF p. 18

study_design.comment: Longitudinal pre-post regulatory intervention evaluation across municipalities served by Copasa-MG/Copanor; the authors explicitly note that no untreated counterfactual group is available, precluding difference-in-differences estimation.
study_design.value: Uncontrolled before-and-after longitudinal municipal panel study using non-parametric paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and generalized least squares (GLS) random-effects panel regressions with White period robust standard errors (2020-2021 main panel and 2018-2021 robustness panel)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section 1; PDF pp. 11-13, Sections 4.1-4.4; PDF p. 20, Section 7
